findings.reason: a worker confined to the two declared paths could make the delivery measure build its tree in the job and still leave the evidence and armed-measure paths holding 1.59 GB per landing on the fleet node, so the gate would pass with the incident unrepaired.
findings.text: the write paths are `reckon/crew/landing_measure.py` and `reckon/crew/queue_landing.py`, but two further callers hold a fleet-node base tree across a partition wait and are where the incident's trees come from: `promotion_evidence._measured_control` (promotion_evidence.py:1649) and the armed-observation path (promotion_records.py:1237) each open `with landing_measure.base_checkout(...)` on the fleet node and then call `control_mutation_observation` / `armed_observations`, which the plan itself says run on the measure partition via `sbatch --wait` (landing_measure.py:1469-1471) — and the incident's four trees were held by a lander and a hand-run `crew complete` while a job ran on all_debug, the exact shape of those two sites

findings.reason: without the declared wait the 24-hour measurement can be dispatched at full width beside s48 and record a day of refused launches as the fleet's behaviour, which is the measurement §10 exists to take.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` states §10's waits as s4-s9, s11-s29, s43, s46 and s47, and omits s48, although a day of landings on the fleet cannot be measured while every queued launch is refused with `tmp-headroom-refusal`, which is precisely the condition s48 removes

findings.reason: the same defect the earlier answer to wiring-1 repaired — a followup that counts the remaining sections wrong — has been reintroduced by adding s48 without extending the followup.
findings.text: the one open followup, f-dwl-s47, tells a coordinator the remaining work is "Section 47 and the live-fleet day in section 10", but plan-section-declarations (plan.html:23) now also declares s48 `implementable`, so the chain a coordinator follows to dispatch the rest does not name the section that repairs the condition blocking the fleet

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — both named write paths (`reckon/crew/landing_measure.py`, `reckon/crew/queue_landing.py`) exist at the reviewed blob; the test file is one the node is to add, the scratch prefix `landing-base-` is the one `base_checkout` creates (landing_measure.py:1658), and the `tmp-headroom-refusal` string with its 5 GiB floor is `dispatch_launch.TmpHeadroomError` (dispatch_launch.py:899-905), consistent with the recorded 5.37 GB.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — s48 names one concrete test file, three measurable cases, an arm-log shape a later reader can check, and a negative control ("at the base revision, the first case must fail, with a base tree held under the scratch root while the job runs"); that control can fail at this base, since `queue_landing._measure_delivery` opens `candidate_checkout` (queue_landing.py:1211) and `base_checkout` (queue_landing.py:1220) on the fleet node and holds both across `measure_run`'s `sbatch --wait` submission (`partition_submission` builds `sbatch --wait` at landing_measure.py:902).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the arms' logs are declared under the run directory (`landing-measure/`), the durable per-run location the existing measure already writes, not a node-local scratch path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s48 names an invariant and a scratch prefix as they read.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s48 carries one invariant: a landing must not hold a fleet-node base tree while its measurement runs elsewhere, with the fleet-node case bounded to one tree as the same invariant.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the plan's own declaration meta at plan.html:24 never lists s48, so §10, the 24-hour live-fleet measurement, may be dispatched while the /tmp refusal s48 repairs is still shipped, and the open driving followup f-dwl-s47 (plan.html:388) still names only §47 and §10 as remaining work.
